rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This problem-solving plan starts by connecting the known power rule to the new product rule through one complete example. Two short teaching sessions establish the rule and procedure, followed by independent application and a final verification session. Each session fits a 15-minute availability window and keeps one main action prominent.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Recognize when the product rule is needed and understand each part of the formula.
sessions.amountLabel: Product rule formula and one complete worked derivative
completionEvidence: Explain why differentiating a product requires two terms.
Apply the formula alongside one complete example.

sessions.title: Apply the Procedure with Guidance
sessions.objective: Use the product rule step by step on a similar expression.
contentTargets: Assigning f, g, f', and g' before substitution
completionEvidence: Construct the four required parts for a given product.
Solve one derivative using the product rule with prompts.

sessions.title: Differentiate Products Independently
sessions.objective: Select and apply the product rule without step prompts.
completionEvidence: Recall the product rule without assistance.
Solve two product derivatives and simplify the results.

sessions.title: Verify Independent Use
sessions.objective: Distinguish product-rule problems from power-rule problems and repair any remaining error.
sessions.amountLabel: One rule-selection check and one final derivative
contentTargets: Choosing between the product rule and power rule
completionEvidence: Classify expressions by the differentiation rule they require.
Demonstrate an accurate independent solution to one product-rule problem.

essentialIdeas: The product rule says the derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second.

activities.label: explain the rule
activities.title: Say the rule in your own words
activities.body: Explain the rule from memory in one or two sentences.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is f'g + fg'.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and shows that each factor gets differentiated once.

activities.label: repair the gap
activities.title: Fix the missing second term
activities.body: Use the feedback to correct the rule in one short revision.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Leaving out one term and treating a product like it has only one derivative part.
activities.concept: The product rule needs two terms, not one.
activities.correctAnswer: The product rule is (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
activities.feedback: The correction must include both parts. If only one factor is differentiated, the rule is incomplete.

activities.label: reexplain the rule
activities.title: Explain it again clearly
activities.body: Explain the rule again without copying the model.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate the first factor and multiply by the second, then add the first factor times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: A strong explanation includes both terms and the reason the rule makes two pieces.

activities.label: recognize the rule
activities.title: Which rule fits this expression?
activities.body: Choose the best rule for a product of two changing factors.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first
activities.feedback: A product of two functions needs the product rule, not the power rule, constant rule, or quotient rule.
